claims.head: Strength against strength
claims.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for the power play, and the Penguins are near the top of the league at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Stars’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
claims.call: The Stars’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.5 expected goals per 60 against the Penguins.
claims.nums: Dallas 3rd for the power play (9.0 expected goals per 60) · Pittsburgh 6th for the penalty kill
claims.gist: It’s strength against strength: the Stars for the power play, the Penguins at the penalty kill.

claims.head: The Penguins give up good looks, and the Stars take them
claims.call: The Stars’ average shot has at least their usual 6.7% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Penguins have struggled to prevent dangerous shots, and the Stars don’t waste many.
claims.nums: Dallas 4th for shot quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Pittsburgh 27th for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: The Stars make their shots count, and the Penguins allow dangerous ones.

story.head: Strength against strength
paras: The Penguins haven’t won in three. The Stars have won two in a row, the last a 4-0 rout of Buffalo.
It’s strength against strength: the Stars for the power play, the Penguins at the penalty kill. The Stars make their shots count, and the Penguins allow dangerous ones.
